mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved in every weekly mean from -51.4 to -46.3 percent. Continued transit recovery raises the count of discretionary trips into commercial districts, which mechanically lifts RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly mean rose from -51.4 at t-3w to -46.3 at t-0w with no reversal
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below its mean over the last 28 days while TRANSIT keeps improving week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has dropped from 6.0 to 4.1 and is approaching its neutral level. Once the weekly mean falls below +4.5, time released from staying at home converts into weekday shopping trips and RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +4.5 percent
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically from 6.0 at t-3w to 4.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: Within 14 days of RESIDENTIAL printing below +4.5, RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery (-18.9 to -14.7) and RESIDENTIAL decline (6.0 to 4.1) reinforce each other: commuting creates pass-through retail demand that neither series generates alone, so the joint movement lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves at least 3 points while RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point across the four weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 4.2 points while RESIDENTIAL fell 1.9 points across the snapshot
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES improves and RESIDENTIAL falls jointly, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is no higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-December is the peak of holiday retail spending; the next 28 days contain the Christmas shopping surge while the last 28 days only contained its run-up. PARKS holding near -14 indicates leisure budgets are flowing indoors toward retail venues.
candidate_trigger: calendar weeks fall inside the December holiday shopping window
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC jumped 3.2 points from -8.1 at t-1w to -4.9 at t-0w while PARKS stayed near -14
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averaged over the next 28 days is below its last-28-day mean during the December holiday window.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has climbed steadily to +7.3, above its baseline. Errand routines that normalize grocery trips also normalize adjacent in-person retail trips, so RETAIL_REC rises within one week of the grocery series holding above +6.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean stays above +6.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 4.3 at t-3w to 7.3 at t-0w without a down week
failure_condition: In weeks when GROCERY_PHARM sits above +6.0, RETAIL_REC fails to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The monotone improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is consistent with continuing policy easing. As capacity limits are lifted, retail and recreation venues regain customers, so RETAIL_REC rises over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve across three consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved in each of the last three week-on-week comparisons
failure_condition: Under easing restrictions, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is flat or lower than the last 28 days despite continued TRANSIT and WORKPLACES gains.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rebounded 5.6 points in the latest week while RETAIL_REC gained only 3.2 points over the whole window. Households substituting leisure time toward outdoor recreation divert spending away from indoor retail and recreation venues, pushing RETAIL_REC down over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises at least 4 points while RETAIL_REC gains less than 4 points over the same window
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -19.9 at t-1w to -14.3 at t-0w, a 5.6-point gain
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean whenever PARKS outpaces RETAIL_REC recovery.

mechanism_narrative: The 3.2-point week-on-week rise in RETAIL_REC is the largest single-week gain in the four-week window and reverses three flat weeks. Positive momentum in this series persists for roughly four weeks, so the next 28-day mean stays above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved -9.7, -8.0, -8.1, -4.9 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: After a week-on-week RETAIL_REC gain above 3 points, the next 28-day mean is at or below the prior 28-day mean.
